sentences.text: 1 This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. As per the Notification No.ADM-I/328/25, dated. 23.04.2025, this case is withdrawn from SCCH-07 and re- allocated to SCCH-23.
3.

The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 02.02.2024 at about 4.15 a.m, after loading the goods at Yelachahalli, Hosakote Taluk, the petitioner along with driver of the Tata Ace goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-9063 were returning to their native place and proceeding by observing all traffic rules and regulations and when they reached near Chikkanallal, Hosakote, Bengaluru at that juncture the driver of said Tata Ace lost the control over the vehicle and without seeing the ditch in the center of the road, in order to save the same, took slight turn towards left side and in the mean time the driver of the said vehicle lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the compound wall and caused the accident.
Due to the terrific impact the goods vehicle turn turtle and the petitioner fell down on the ground and sustained severe injuries all over the body.
It is further urged that the petitioner was shifted to SNR Hospital, Kolar, wherein he took first aid and thereafter he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital.
Wherein he was treated as inpatient and was discharged with an advice to take complete bed rest.

It is alleged that he has spent substantial amount towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.

It is specifically urged that the petitioner was working as coolie / cleaner and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m and because of the accident the petitioner is suffering both financially and emotionally.
Further it is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of driver of Tata Ace.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
4. The respondent No.1 though entered appearance through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
5. After service of notice, respondent No.2 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of New Tata Ace Commercial vehicle.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
It is contended that the petitioner was traveling as gratuitous passenger in the goods vehicle, the insurance policy does not cover the risk of gratuitous passengers in goods vehicle.
Negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the petitioner was the solely responsible for cause of accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :

9. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1: The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of Tata Ace for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

It is specific contention of Respondent No.2 is that the offending vehicle is not involved in the accident and further the accident occurred due to the negligence of petitioner himself as such the respondent No.1 is not at all liable to pay any compensation amount.

It is also urged that there is inordinate delay of 2 days that itself vibrantly discloses that the case is foisted so as to wangle the compensation amount from the insurance company and hence prayed to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2.
In support of these contentions the respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Officer as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.

In his chief examination he further stated that as pe Ex.P.9-Discharge Sandeep C vs Santhosha B V on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120687737/

Further the owner of the insured Tata ace goods vehicle has not paid premium to cover the risk of gratuitous passengers in goods vehicle.
11. It is relevant to note that as per the version of the petitioner the accident happened on 02.02.2024 at about 4.15 a.m, the criminal law was set into motion on 05.02.2024 at about 2.30 p.m.
It is vociferously urged that there is an inordinate delay of 3 days and the offending vehicle is falsely implicated so as to wangle the compensation.

It is relevant to note that the petitioner has got exhibited Ex.P.5 being the wound certificate issued by Government Hospital, Hosakote wherein it discloses that the petitioner was taken to hospital and thereafter he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital at Bengaluru.
12. In this regard the petitioner has examined the MRO of NIMHANS hospital as PW.2, he has produced Ex.P.12 IP Record of NIMHANS Hospital.

On perusal of Casualty patient record it is clearly mentioned the date and time of Reg. is mentioned as :
02.02.2024 at about 5.23 p.m.
Hence it is clear that on the date of accident he was admitted to the NIMHANS Hospital and he took treatment.
The medical records discloses that the petitioner was injured in the accident.
In view of contents in Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.12 wound certificate and inpatient record the delay of 3 days is self explanatory.

There is a delay of 3 days and that delay is well explained by the petitioner in this regard it is relevant to relied on the decision reported in Ravi v.
Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226, wherein the Hon'ble Aoex Court has observed as hereunder :
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

entities.text:
Ravi v.
Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."

sentences.text: (Emphasis supplied by me).
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The ratio decidendi laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the instant case.
The petitioner had explained the delay caused.
The petitioner clearly demonstrated as to the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident.
13. The learned counsel for the Insurance Company laid emphasis on the entry made in the discharge summary wherein it is mentioned that 'A/H/o RTA skid and fall" hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
But the fact that deserves notice is that in case sheet of NIMHANS Hospital, in the column the injured person name is clearly mentioned and also clearly mentioned the date and time also.
Generally, not only the victim but also the person who brings him to the hospital would be in trauma.
The possibility of providing improper information at such time cannot be ruled out.

Moreover due to rush of work and constant pressure under which the hospital authorities work,
there might have been some discrepancies in recording the details at the said column.

This entry alone thus cannot be the basis to conclude that the petitioner sustained injuries on account of rash and negligent act of driver of Tata Ace vehicle but not bike hit a ditch and skid and fall.
14. Be that as it may, the IMV inspector has mentioned that he tested insured vehicle and found that its brake system was in order.
He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicle.
Therefore the driver of the Tata Ace did not have sufficient cause to have lost control of his vehicle.

Such being the case, the very fact that he dashed against the compound wall and caused the accident and the said vehicle turn turtle leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle in a rash & negligent manner.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
No independent witness was either produced by the insurer to displace the version of the accident as deposed by the injured claimant.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Tata Ace goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-9063.
15.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 3 SCC 646.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered in the 'Affirmative'.

In order to substantiate the said fact he has not produced any documents to prove the same.

It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2024.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
17. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : Fracture of second cervical vertebra (odontoid fracture type-2).
It is needless to say that the injury is grievous in nature.

The case sheet of NIMHANS hospital (Ex.P.12) indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient from 03.02.2024 to 12.02.2024, in total the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for a period of 10 days.
During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : Internal fixation of C1 and C-2 with pedicle screw and fusion.
18. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.B. Ramesh as PW.3 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 20% of spine which is 10% disability to the whole body.
It is elicited during the course of cross examination PW.3 categorically admitted that he was not treated the petitioner.
He admitted that fractures are united.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctors, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 5%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 5%.

20. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of her stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 2 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.33,000/- (16,500 X 2) under this head.
22. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P9, the petitioner has spent Rs.4,247/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,247/- which is rounded off to Rs.4,300/- towards medical expenses.
23. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '17'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,68,300/- (Rs.16,500 X 12 X 17 X 5/100) is awarded under this head.
24. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES & HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
25. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.10,000/- towards future medical & other incidental expenses.

sentences.text: 27. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
28. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

The plea of the insurance company with whom the Tata Ace vehicle is insured is that it is a goods carrying vehicle and the risk of the persons traveling in the goods vehicle is not covered under the terms & conditions of the policy issued in favour of respondent No.1.

Per contra, the petitioner assert that after loading the goods he returning to native place in a offending vehicle he was working as coolie under the respondent No.1 the said offending Tata Ace vehicle.
During the course of cross examination he categorically admitted that he has not produced any documents to prove he was working as cleaner under respondent No.1.
Pleadings is not evidence, far less proof.

Moreover the elicitation brought out during the course of cross-examination of PW.1 establish the fact that on the fateful day of the occurrence of accident he was traveling as unauthorized occupant in the Tata Tace insured by the respondent No.2.
29.

The law as regards fastening of liability on the insurer to pay compensation for the injuries /
death caused to an occupant of goods carriage vehicle is well settled.

The Act does not provide for carrying of persons in a goods carriage meant for carrying goods and that the owner of such a goods carriage will not be entitled to statutory indemnity against the claim made by the petitioner gratuitous passenger / unauthorized occupant.

In fact, the Act does not enjoin any statutory liability on the owner of the vehicle to get his vehicle insured for any person traveling in a goods carriage and the insurer would have no liability thereto.
This is the statement of law as declared by the Apex Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd V/s Vedwati reported in 2007 ACJ 1043 (SC).

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd V/s Vedwati reported in 2007 ACJ 1043 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Reliance is also placed on the decision reported in 2005 ACJ 721 between National Insurance Co.Ltd V/s Bommiti Subbhayamma and others, wherein the law laid down was that : 'Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 147(1) - Motor Insurance- Goods vehicle - Passenger risk - Gratuitous passenger - Liability of insurance company - Death of gratuitous passenger in truck when it met with accident - Tribunal allowed compensation but exempted the insurance company from liability - High Court in appeal affixed liability on the insurance company - Whether the insurance company is liable - Held : No,
claimants entitled to recover award compensation from owner of vehicle'.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd V/s Bommiti Subbhayamma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 30. In the light of the ratio deducible from the decisions cited supra, as the risk of the petitioner (who were traveling as unauthorized occupant in the Tata Ace vehicle on the day of accident) was not covered under ExR.2-Policy, liability cannot be foisted on the insurance company.

Accordingly,
the petition deserves to be dismissed against respondent No.2 (the insurer of the Tata Ace goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-9063).

Consequently, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said Tata Ace vehicle is liable to pay the award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'..

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,27,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 / owner of Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-9063 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
The petition is dismissed against respondent No.2/insurer of Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-9063.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.
If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The ratio decidendi laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the instant case.
Such being the case, the very fact that he dashed against the compound wall and caused the accident and the said vehicle turn turtle leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle in a rash & negligent manner.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
No independent witness was either produced by the insurer to displace the version of the accident as deposed by the injured claimant.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 3 SCC 646.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctors, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 5%, cannot be ruled out.

The law as regards fastening of liability on the insurer to pay compensation for the injuries /
death caused to an occupant of goods carriage vehicle is well settled.
The Act does not provide for carrying of persons in a goods carriage meant for carrying goods and that the owner of such a goods carriage will not be entitled to statutory indemnity against the claim made by the petitioner gratuitous passenger / unauthorized occupant.
In fact, the Act does not enjoin any statutory liability on the owner of the vehicle to get his vehicle insured for any person traveling in a goods carriage and the insurer would have no liability thereto.
This is the statement of law as declared by the Apex Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd V/s Vedwati reported in 2007 ACJ 1043 (SC).
Consequently, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said Tata Ace vehicle is liable to pay the award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,27,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 / owner of Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-9063 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
The petition is dismissed against respondent No.2/insurer of Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-9063.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
